description: Composite EBSD figure with two columns of boundary/grain-structure maps, both showing an Fe–8% Al low density steel after hot torsion (ε = 2) at 1100 °C. Left column, labelled "a. Ė = 5 s⁻¹", contains two stacked maps: the upper map is dominated by large equiaxed grains outlined by black lines with a sparse network of red lines; the lower map shows elongated, band-like features in which fine grains and red boundaries decorate shear bands, plus a large elongated grain at the top. Right column, labelled "b. Ė = 10 s⁻¹", repeats the arrangement: an upper map of equiaxed grains with relatively straight black boundaries and numerous red boundary segments, and a lower map showing a strongly banded, elongated structure with a high density of red lines within the band. Each panel carries a 500 µm scale bar and black arrows at the top-left and bottom-right marking the torsion/shear direction. No orientation colour key, step size or boundary-misorientation criterion is printed. The figure's argument is that the same torsion strain produces different microstructures at the two strain rates: at 5 s⁻¹ the coarse grains persist with localised banding, whereas at 10 s⁻¹ the banded, boundary-decorated structure is more pronounced, consistent with a changing dynamic-recrystallization mechanism.

observations.observation: The figure contains four EBSD maps arranged in two labelled columns, 'a. Ė = 5 s⁻¹' and 'b. Ė = 10 s⁻¹', each column holding two stacked maps.
Both columns carry a 500 µm scale bar.
Black arrows at the top-left and bottom-right of each map mark the torsion shear direction.
Grain boundaries are rendered as two line colours, black and red; no legend or misorientation criterion is printed to define them.
In the (a) Ė = 5 s⁻¹ column, the upper map shows large equiaxed grains with only sparse red boundary segments.
In the (a) column, the lower map shows an elongated band of fine grains with densely spaced red boundaries, plus one large elongated grain.
In the (b) Ė = 10 s⁻¹ column, the upper map shows equiaxed grains outlined with relatively straight black boundaries and many red boundary segments.
In the (b) column, the lower map shows a strong elongated band containing a high density of fine red-marked boundaries.
No numerical grain size, misorientation angle or fraction-recrystallized value is printed on any panel.
The caption states the samples were deformed by torsion at ε = 2 and 1100 °C at strain rates of 5 s⁻¹ and 10 s⁻¹.
The caption identifies the maps as EBSD maps of the deformed microstructures.
The citing text states that EBSD maps illustrating the microstructures of torsion-deformed samples are given in this figure.

subfigures.description: Column labelled 'a. Ė = 5 s⁻¹', containing two stacked EBSD maps with a 500 µm scale bar and shear-direction arrows. Upper map: large equiaxed grains drawn with black boundary lines, with a sparse set of red boundary segments. Lower map: a strongly elongated grain at top plus a band of fine grains and dense red boundary segments running diagonally, interpreted as a shear band/deformation band.

Column labelled 'b. Ė = 10 s⁻¹', containing two stacked EBSD maps with a 500 µm scale bar and shear-direction arrows. Upper map: equiaxed grains with straight black boundaries and abundant red boundary segments outlining grains. Lower map: a pronounced elongated band containing a high density of fine, red-marked boundaries, surrounded by coarse grains.
